answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by pricing the one thing a farm cannot clone: a sponsor's reputation. Each newcomer needs three vouchers from unrelated operators, each juniper-thin and snapping if its referrer ever backs a proven clone. Vouchers are capped per sponsor, so reputation cannot be bulk-bought; when clean sponsors run dry a farm must post umber-dark collateral, locked for epochs and slashed on detection. The shale layer is the audit: random panels re-check vouchees later and each failure charges the whole voucher chain, so cost per head grows while yield stays flat.
